board_anchors_verified: J257 Foundation 01/02 and Higher 03/04; Breadth and Depth in biology; each 90 marks, 1 hour 45 minutes, 50%; both papers assess all eight chapters; practicals are PAGs. No lesson in this unit asserts a paper structure, so nothing needed correcting.
chapter_mapping: L1-L2 = Chapter B4 (B4.1, B4.2 partly, B4.3, B4.4, B4.5); L3-L5 = Chapter B5 (B5.1 partly, B5.2, B5.3 partly, B5.4, B5.5, B5.6 partly).

findings.claim: Key Fact: "Both types occur in the absence of sufficient oxygen."
findings.truth: Only the two forms of anaerobic respiration happen when oxygen is short. Aerobic respiration needs oxygen. As written the sentence follows a comparison of aerobic and anaerobic, so it reads as a misconception.
findings.evidence: spec B4.1 narrative: "In conditions of low or no oxygen ... anaerobic respiration occurs"; B4.1.1

findings.claim: Q5 type "3 marks — Explain (HT)" on a question about why muscle cells hold many mitochondria.
findings.truth: B4.1.3 is not in bold in the bold-preserved spec, so it is assessed at both tiers. The (HT) flag is wrong.

findings.claim: Q4 type "4 marks — Multi-Step Calculation".
findings.truth: The question asks the student to explain why breathing rate stays high after exercise. There is no calculation.

findings.claim: "During mitosis, a cell first copies all of its DNA (so each chromosome exists in duplicate), then divides".
findings.truth: DNA is copied during interphase, before mitosis. During mitosis the chromosome copies separate, the nucleus divides and the cell divides. The lesson's own next paragraph says interphase is when DNA is replicated, so the article contradicts itself.
findings.evidence: spec B4.3 narrative and B4.3.1a: "During interphase the cell grows larger ... and each chromosome is copied; then during mitosis the chromosome copies separate"

findings.claim: A higher-only wrapper hides the whole "Plant Hormones: Auxin and Tropisms" section from Foundation students.
findings.truth: B4.4.1a (auxins in phototropisms and gravitropisms) is NOT bold, so it is assessed at both tiers; B4.4 is separate-science only, which this subject is. The wrapper was used to mean separate-only. Only the commercial-use box (gibberellins, ethene, human use of plant hormones) is genuinely Higher, so the wrapper is narrowed onto it.
findings.evidence: spec B4.4.1a (not bold); B4.4.2 and B4.4.3 bold in biology-b-21c-J257-bold.md

findings.claim: The meristem paragraph teaches rooting powder and synthetic plant hormones with no tier flag.
findings.truth: Using plant hormones to control growth is B4.4.3, which is bold (Higher only). The sentence sits in a both-tier paragraph, so it takes an inline tag rather than a wrapper.

findings.claim: Seven items flag auxin, phototropism and gravitropism as "(Higher only)" / "(HT)" / "(Higher)": the takeaway, the exam tip, practice Q3 and Q5 (text and type) and flashcards 7, 8 and 9.
findings.truth: B4.4.1a is not bold, so all of this is both-tier. Flags removed. Flashcard 10 (commercial use of synthetic auxin) keeps its (Higher) tag because B4.4.3 is bold.

findings.claim: Q3 type "4 marks — Required Practical Method" on "Describe how the alveoli are adapted to maximise the rate of gas exchange."
findings.truth: "Required practical" is AQA wording. OCR Twenty First Century Science uses PAGs. The question is also not a practical method question at all.
findings.evidence: spec practical work sections list PAG1-PAG8; no "required practical" anywhere in J257

findings.claim: Q5 type "3 marks — Explain (HT)" on active transport at root hairs versus diffusion of oxygen.
findings.truth: B5.1.2 is not bold, so this is both-tier.

findings.claim: "you must mention the concentration gradient is reversed".
findings.truth: Active transport moves substances against the gradient. The gradient itself is not reversed. A student writing "the gradient is reversed" would not be describing active transport correctly.
findings.evidence: spec B5.1 narrative: "other substances by active transport"; settled definition

findings.claim: The brain section names the "cerebrum" and the "medulla oblongata".
findings.truth: B5.2.4 names the cerebral cortex (intelligence, memory, language and consciousness), the cerebellum (conscious movement) and the brain stem (regulation of heart and breathing rate). The article and glossary now use the spec terms and keep the familiar names alongside.

findings.claim: "Techniques such as MRI scanning allow scientists to observe which brain regions are active during different tasks".
findings.truth: Plain MRI images structure. Activity mapping uses functional MRI, which is the technique the spec names.
findings.evidence: spec B5.2 narrative (bold): "functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI)"

findings.claim: Q5 type "3 marks — Explain (HT)" on the myelinated axon.
findings.truth: B5.2.2 is not bold, so this is both-tier.

findings.claim: Q5 mark scheme requires "the impulse jumps between gaps in the sheath (nodes of Ranvier)" for the third mark.
findings.truth: Saltatory conduction and nodes of Ranvier are beyond J257. The spec asks only that the fatty sheath increases transmission speed, and says learners are not expected to explain impulse transmission in terms of membrane potentials. A student answering to spec would lose the mark.
findings.evidence: spec B5.2 narrative: "Most axons have a fatty sheath to increase impulse transmission speed"; B5.2.2 note

findings.claim: Q4 type "4 marks — Compare or Contrast" on "explain why their hand moved before they felt pain".
findings.truth: The question asks for an explanation, not a comparison.

findings.claim: Q6 mark scheme credits "conditioned reflexes can be overridden with practice ... suggesting reflexes are not entirely automatic".
findings.truth: A conditioned reflex is a learned response, not an overridden one. The spec's idea is that the brain can modify a reflex response through a neuron to the motor neuron of the reflex arc, for example to stop us dropping a hot object.

findings.claim: "For synapse questions, describe three steps" followed by four stages.
findings.truth: Four stages are listed: impulse arrives, transmitter released, binds to receptors, new impulse.

findings.claim: A higher-only wrapper hides the whole thermoregulation section, including sweating, vasodilation, vasoconstriction and shivering.
findings.truth: B5.4.2a (the function of the skin in temperature control, including sweating, hair erection and blood flow) is not bold, so it is both-tier. Only the receptors / hypothalamic processing / negative-feedback framing is bold (B5.4.3). The wrapper is narrowed onto the negative-feedback paragraph and the hypothalamus sentence takes an inline tag.

findings.claim: The four-hormone menstrual cycle interaction is wrapped as higher-only in the article, but the takeaway, practice Q4, knowledge check 4 and flashcards 6, 7 and 8 all teach it with no tier flag.
findings.truth: B5.5.2 and the whole FSH/oestrogen/LH/progesterone bullet list are bold, so they are Higher only. Flags added so Foundation students are not revising material they cannot be examined on. Contraception (B5.5.3) stays untagged because it is both-tier.
findings.evidence: spec B5.5.2 and B5.5 narrative bullets (bold); B5.5.1 and B5.5.3 not bold

findings.claim: Q4 type "4 marks — Compare or Contrast" on "Explain how the four hormones ... interact".
findings.truth: The question asks for an explanation, not a comparison.

findings.claim: Two correct Higher flags used the suffix form "(Higher only)" while the new flags use the house prefix.
findings.truth: Both moved to the "(Higher tier)" prefix so the lesson is consistent. The flags themselves were right (B5.4.6 is bold).

findings.claim: Match stem: "Match each hormone to its role in blood glucose regulation:" with ADH as one of the three hormones.
findings.truth: ADH controls water balance, not blood glucose, so the stem contradicts its own items. Stem widened, and ADH tagged (Higher) to match the glucagon entry beside it.
findings.evidence: spec B5.4.6 (ADH, bold) vs B5.6.1-2 (blood sugar)

findings.claim: Chapter mapping and coverage. The five lessons map to Chapter B4 (Using food and controlling growth) and Chapter B5 (The human body - staying alive). This is the only unit in separate-sciences-ocr-b that covers B4 and B5 (the siblings are you-and-your-genes = B1, keeping-healthy = B2, life-on-earth-ecosystems = B3/B6), so anything absent here is absent from the subject.
findings.truth: Outcomes taught nowhere in the unit, all both-tier unless marked. B4.2.1 electron microscopy and B4.2.2 scale / estimation / standard form (2c Higher). B4.3.2 cancer as uncontrolled division and B4.3.3 meiosis (both may sit in the B1 or B2 units - check before building). B4.4.2 ethene (gibberellins are mentioned; ethene is not) - Higher. B5.1.4 heart structure (cardiac muscle, chambers, valves). B5.1.5 arteries, veins and capillaries. B5.1.7 and B5.1.8 surface area to volume ratio and calculating it. B5.3.2 thyroxine and adrenaline, thyroxine as negative feedback - Higher. B5.4.2a hair erection. B5.6.4a eye structures (cornea, iris, lens, ciliary muscle, retina) with ray diagrams and B5.6.5 short sight, long sight and cataracts. B5.6.6 limits on treating nervous system damage - Higher, only glanced at in L2. No PAG practical (PAG1 mitosis, PAG5 respiration in yeast, PAG6 phototropism / reflexes / temperature control / pupil response) is described anywhere. Options: (a) add two lessons - one on the heart, blood vessels and surface area to volume, one on the eye and its defects - plus a thyroxine and adrenaline section in L5 and a cell-structures and microscopy section in L1; (b) accept the gaps and record them on the subject build plan. Recommendation: (a); the heart, blood vessels, surface area to volume and the eye are core both-tier content on every paper.
findings.evidence: spec B4.2, B4.3.2, B4.3.3, B4.4.2, B5.1.4, B5.1.5, B5.1.7, B5.1.8, B5.3.2, B5.4.2a, B5.6.4, B5.6.5, B5.6.6; grep of raw/L01-L05 finds no ventricle, atrium, valve, artery, cornea, ciliary, cataract, thyroxine, adrenaline, magnification or surface-area-to-volume text
findings.ruling: Structural gap: heart, blood vessels, SA:V, eye/defects, thyroxine/adrenaline, microscopy, PAGs untaught anywhere in separate-sciences-ocr-b. Needs two new lessons + two sections; Tom decision. Recorded in corpus_notes.

findings.claim: L3 and L5 define and test osmosis in terms of "water potential" throughout: the osmosis definition, the glossary, knowledge check 4 in L3, the ADH key fact, the L5 exam tip and two L5 flashcards.
findings.truth: The spec says learners are not expected to discuss water potential. The board's own language is water moving by osmosis and blood plasma at the correct concentration to prevent cells shrinking or bursting. Options: (a) leave it - it is not wrong, only above the required level; (b) re-word to "more dilute / more concentrated solution" across both lessons, which touches roughly a dozen narration blocks and needs re-narration. Recommendation: (b) at the next narration pass for these two lessons, not as a standalone edit.
findings.evidence: spec B5.4.4 note: "Learners are not expected to discuss water potential"; B5.1 narrative
findings.ruling: Water-potential language is above spec level but not wrong; re-word L3/L5 to dilute/concentrated at the next narration pass. Recorded in corpus_notes.

findings.claim: The thermoregulation section covers sweating, vasodilation, vasoconstriction and shivering but not hair erection.
findings.truth: B5.4.2a names sweating, hair erection and blood flow. Adding it means adding a list item, which would add a narration block, so it is left for the next content pass.

findings.claim: Once the Higher wrapper on the four-hormone list is respected, a Foundation student sees only one sentence on the menstrual cycle before the contraception box.
findings.truth: B5.5.1 (describe the role of hormones in human reproduction, including control of the menstrual cycle) is both-tier, so Foundation needs a little more than one sentence. The wrapper itself is correct, so this is a content-thickness point, not a tier error.

findings.claim: L3 and L4 descriptions both end with the template sentence "Key concepts and applications explained." The L3 description is exactly 100 characters, which is at the validator limit.
findings.truth: Both replaced with a written description of what the lesson covers. L3 drops to 92 characters.
findings.evidence: raw/L03.txt and raw/L04.txt descriptions; house rule: lesson description under 100 characters

summary: All five lessons carried findings: 2 HIGH (DNA copied 'during mitosis'; an AQA 'Required Practical Method' question type), 18 MEDIUM and 5 LOW, with 45 surgical edits. The dominant fault is the tier wrapper running both ways - higher-only used to mean separate-only over auxin/tropisms (L2) and the whole thermoregulation section (L5), while genuinely Higher menstrual-cycle content leaked untagged into takeaways, practice, knowledge checks and flashcards. Two unit-level ADJUDICATEs: a large block of both-tier B4/B5 outcomes (heart, blood vessels, surface area to volume, the eye, thyroxine/adrenaline, electron microscopy) is taught nowhere in the subject, and both L3 and L5 teach osmosis in water-potential language the spec excludes.
